content.title: What are Control Statements and Loops?
content.description: Control statements determine the flow of execution in a Java program, while loops allow a block of code to execute repeatedly until a specified condition is met.

content.content: Programs often need to make decisions or repeat tasks. Java provides control statements such as if, if-else, switch, and loops like for, while, and do-while to handle these situations efficiently.

content.title: Why Control Statements?
content.content: Without control statements, programs would execute every statement sequentially without making decisions or repeating operations.
Decision-Making Statements
Decision-making statements execute different blocks of code depending on whether a condition evaluates to true or false.

items.question: if Statement
items.answer: Executes a block only if the condition is true.

items.question: if-else Statement
items.answer: Executes one block when the condition is true and another when it is false.

items.question: else-if Ladder
items.answer: Checks multiple conditions one after another.

items.question: switch Statement
items.answer: Selects one block from multiple possible choices.

content.content: if Statement
The if statement is the simplest decision-making statement. It executes its block only when the specified condition evaluates to true.

content.title: if Statement Example

content.content: if-else Statement
The if-else statement provides two execution paths depending on the result of the condition.
switch Statement
The switch statement is useful when a variable can have multiple predefined values. It improves readability compared to long else-if ladders.

content.title: switch Example
Remember
content.content: Always use break in a switch statement unless intentional fall-through behavior is required.
Loops in Java
Loops repeatedly execute a block of code while a condition remains true. They eliminate repetitive coding and improve efficiency.

items.question: for Loop
items.answer: Best when the number of iterations is known.

items.question: while Loop
items.answer: Best when the number of iterations is unknown.

items.question: do-while Loop
items.answer: Executes the loop body at least once before checking the condition.

content.content: for Loop
The for loop combines initialization, condition checking, and update in a single statement, making it ideal for counting loops.
while Loop
The while loop checks the condition before each iteration. If the condition is false initially, the loop body is never executed.
do-while Loop
The do-while loop executes its body first and checks the condition afterward, ensuring at least one execution.
Loop Control Statements
Java provides special statements to alter the normal flow of loops.

content.title: break and continue

content.content: Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Traffic Signals
content.content: A traffic signal controls when vehicles should stop, move, or wait. Similarly, control statements decide which part of a program should execute, while loops repeatedly allow vehicles (instructions) to pass until the condition changes.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Questions on if-else, switch, loop execution order, break, continue, and nested loops are very common in Java interviews and coding assessments.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Why does an infinite loop occur?
items.answer: Because the loop condition never becomes false or the loop variable is not updated.

items.question: Why does switch execute multiple cases?
items.answer: Because the break statement is missing.

items.question: When should you use do-while?
items.answer: When the loop body must execute at least once regardless of the condition.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Use if for simple decisions, switch for multiple fixed choices, for when iterations are known, while for unknown iterations, and do-while when at least one execution is required.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: if and switch are decision-making statements.
for, while, and do-while are looping statements.
break exits a loop or switch.
continue skips the current loop iteration.
